messages:
maria: Hey team — trying to provision a new GPU nodepool in europe-west3 but hitting quota failures and weird fragmentation across AZs. Can we discuss sizing + cooldown strategy?
aj: Which SKU and target size? quota message?
maria: Requesting 12 x A10G (n1-standard-32 + a10g), 3 AZ spread (a/b/c). Cloud returned: "Quota exceeded for resource 'GPUS' in region 'europe-west3'" and some AZs report "INSUFFICIENT_CAPACITY".
lucas: Two thoughts: (1) regional quota vs per-AZ availability — some providers split GPUs into AZ pools so spread=3 can increase INS capacity risk, (2) autoscaler cooldown can cause rapid scale-up/scale-down chatter if min/max not tuned.
sophie: Agreed. Also double-check our node provisioning cooldown in cluster-autoscaler config — we recently lowered scaleDownDelay which might be too aggressive for GPU workloads (long startup + warm-up).
infra-bot: cluster-autoscaler: scale up triggered for deployment/encoder, needed 4 nodes; attempt to create 4 instances in europe-west3-b failed: INSUFFICIENT_CAPACITY.
aj: Maybe provision with less AZ spread initially (2 AZs) to reduce fragmentation, then expand after we secure quota. Tradeoff: slightly less fault tolerance.
maria: What's the recommended min/max and cooldown for GPU pools? We don't want pods bouncing between nodes.
ryan: For GPU pools running long-running encoder jobs, we use min=1, max=12, scale_up_delay=1m, scale_down_delay=20m, and node-provisioning-cooldown=10m in CA. Also set pod disruption budgets to avoid evict storms.
lucas: Also consider adding startup taint like node.kubernetes.io/gpu-startup: "true" and remove it via a daemon once the node is healthy; prevents scheduling onto half-configured nodes.
sophie: On cost/capacity: preemptible/spot would cut cost but increases evictions. For batch encoders spot is fine; for low-latency dedicated routes use reserved. Can create a mixed nodepool: 8 spot + 4 on-demand.
maria: Cloud quota teams said they can increase regional GPU quota but it takes ~48 hours. In the meantime we need a workaround to unblock testing.
aj: Workaround: create smaller nodepool in europe-west3-a with 2 A10G (AZ with capacity), and point lower-priority batch jobs there. Configure node affinity for batch.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: created nodepool gpu-temp-ew3a (size=2, type=a10g). kube events: Pod encoder-xyz pending due to Insufficient GPUs in cluster.
ryan: Also bump node provisioning backoff to 8m to avoid hammering cloud API and hitting quota limits during retries.
lucas: Ops checklist: 1) Reduce AZ spread to 2 for initial pool 2) Create mixed spot/on-demand profile 3) Set scale_down_delay >= 15m 4) Add startup taint + post-start hook 5) Request quota increase (48h).
sophie: I'll draft the terraform change for the nodepool and add a canary label so we can route traffic.
maria: Can someone set the request for quota increase? I filed a ticket but need infra team owner.
aj: I can own the quota request. I'll attach expected usage numbers and cost estimate.
devops-oncall: Heads-up: if we reduce AZ spread, update our SLA doc and update oncall runbook for AZ outage tests.
maria: Thanks — plan for now: aj will submit quota request + create the temp 2-AZ nodepool; sophie will push terraform change; lucas/ryan will update autoscaler cooldown & taints. We'll reconvene after quota response. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: ticket-1234 created: GPU quota increase request (europe-west3) — owner: aj — ETA: 48h
ryan: One more note — set node-kubelet eviction threshold memory to avoid OOMs when GPU drivers initialize (we saw kubelet evicting pods during driver install last month).
maria: Good catch. I'll include that in the terraform module.
aj: I'll post the terraform diff once ready.
lu cas: small nit: ensure GPU driver daemonset tolerations match the startup taint or the node never becomes schedulable.
sophie: Will do.
maria: Thanks all — leaving the thread open until quota is granted and temp pool stabilized.
